vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: food
Version: 1.0.0

The OpenClaw skill bundle 'food' appears benign. The `SKILL.md` and `processing.md` files contain detailed instructions for an AI agent to absorb, classify, and organize food-related input, build a personal database, and provide insights. All instructions are directly aligned with the stated purpose of a 'Food Tracker' and do not contain any evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts designed to subvert the agent for harmful purposes. The skill's functionality is consistent with its description.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions are coherent with a food-tracking purpose, but it is broad about persistent storage of personal and health-related data and omits details about where/how data is stored or processed.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill ingests photos/text of meals, labels, recipes and builds a personal food database. There are no unrelated required binaries, environment variables, or installs that would be out of scope for a food tracker.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and processing.md specify OCR, photo processing, classification, and permanent storage of preferences (e.g., allergies). The instructions do not instruct reading unrelated system files or environment variables, nor do they reference external endpoints, but they give the agent broad discretion ('Absorbs ANY food input') and lack limits on what is stored, retention, or sharing—this raises privacy concerns because dietary and allergy information can be sensitive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest install risk. Nothing is downloaded or written to disk at install time by the skill package itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested. The skill does not ask for unrelated secrets or permissions in its manifest.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly requests permanent storage of preferences and building a personal database. It is not marked always:true (so not force-included), but model invocation is allowed (normal). The manifest does not say where data will be stored, for how long, or whether it will be transmitted off-device — this uncertainty increases privacy risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (track and organize food inputs) and does not request credentials or install code, but it will collect and permanently store personal/health-related information (allergies, eating patterns, photos). Before installing or enabling autonomous use: 1) Ask where data is stored (local vs cloud), how long it is retained, and whether images or nutrition OCR are sent to third-party services; 2) Confirm whether you can delete or export all stored data and clear 'remembered' preferences; 3) Check what permissions the agent will request (camera/photo access, device storage, cloud uploads) and limit them if possible; 4) Test with non-sensitive or dummy data first; 5) If you care about strict privacy, require that image/OCR processing be local or that the developer publish a clear privacy policy. If the developer cannot answer where data is stored and whether it is shared, treat the skill as higher-risk and avoid storing real allergy/medical info.
